title: One WCS per setup: the browser shows a single WCS node, G54-G59 is only the setup's post label

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
Reported by the maintainer (2026-11-08), on the #331 / #329 UI:

> the multiple WCS is not necessary.. it should only be one WCS - and the "name" of it is set in the setups where "Work offset <drop G54>" for example. But it should not be possible to have multiple work offsets in one setup. That will confuse the crap out of people. So G55-59 in the browser tree should be removed and the G54 there should be called WCS.. And the G54-G59 assignment is just a label for the post processor to write the correct code in the output.

## What happens
The browser tree's Setup section lists six work-offset rows, **G54** placed and **G55 ... G59 "not placed"** (one WCS entity per slot, `setup::wcs_entity_name` / the WCS slot entities), each placeable with its own origin. So a document (and a setup) can carry several placed work offsets, and the user has to understand which one a setup posts.

## What it should be
- **One WCS per setup.** Each setup has exactly one work coordinate system - one origin (and, with #326, the part's alignment in that frame). It is shown in the browser as a single node named **WCS** (under its setup), never G54..G59 rows.
- **G54-G59 is only the post label.** The setup's "Work offset" dropdown on the Setups page (G54..G59, #196/#329) just chooses which word the post processor writes for that setup's WCS. It does not select between several stored origins.
- It must be impossible to have several work offsets in one setup.

## Done means
- The browser shows one **WCS** node per setup (no G55-G59 rows, no "not placed" slots); selecting it edits that setup's WCS origin (3-2-1 align, numeric origin, Origin ribbon cell) through the existing undoable commands.
- The model: one WCS origin per setup; the slot is a label on the setup (`SetupDef.work_offset`), read by the post via `setup::wcs_slot`. Remove (or migrate away) the per-slot WCS entities: a project that placed several slot entities migrates each setup's posted slot's origin onto that setup's WCS; other placed slots that no setup posts are dropped with a load note, and a setup whose ops reached two different placed origins is refused by name (never silently re-pointed). Bump the project version.
- The two-setups-same-word refusal (#196) stays: two setups writing the same G5x word with different origins into one NC file is still refused.
- Setup sheet, viewport chip, heights page and MCP all speak of the setup's WCS, labelled with its word (e.g. "WCS (G55)" where the word matters, plain "WCS" in the tree).
- Tests: browser shows one WCS per setup; migration (single placed slot, several placed slots one posted, conflicting) ; posting byte-identical for single-WCS documents; undo of WCS edits; regenerate the shell snapshots.

Part of the multi-setup chain (#308). Builds on #196 (PR #328), #329 (PR #331), #315 (PR #325); related #326 (PR #341), #330.
